commonPoints: The R6 and R6 Mark II use the standard 1/4-20 socket, so any camera tripod fits
Carbon fiber saves weight and damps vibration better than aluminum; aluminum is cheaper
Pick a load rating comfortably above camera plus lens
Arca-Swiss compatible plates let you share plates and use an L-bracket
Travel tripods trade stiffness for packed size; heavy telephotos want bigger legs

ourGain.point: Kit weights from Canon: R6 Mark II 670 g with card and battery; + RF 24-105 F4L (700 g) = 1,370 g; + RF 70-200 F2.8L (1,070 g) = 1,740 g; + RF 100-500 with ring (1,530 g) = 2,200 g. Headroom with the 100-500 kit: Benro Slim 4 kg = 1.8x; Peak Design 9.1 kg and Befree 9 kg = about 4.1x; Leofoto and Vanguard 10 kg = about 4.5x.
Column-down height compared: Vanguard 55.6 in, Leofoto legs 51.97 in with no column, Peak Design 51.25 in, Befree 50.4 in, Benro 48.4 in; only the Vanguard stays above 55 in without raising a column.
ourGain.source: Maker and B&H spec pages listed in sources

ourGain.point: Chooser by lens and trip: 24-105 and flights = Peak Design (or Befree to save money); landscapes and wind with an L-bracket = Leofoto LS-284CX; 100-500 or macro at home = Vanguard Alta Pro G2; lightest budget hiking kit with a 24-105 or primes = Benro Slim.

DPReview advice to buy 50% more load than your heaviest kit and avoid 5-section legs with sub-16mm tubes, applied to each pick: all clear 1.5x with the 100-500 kit; the Peak Design is the only 5-section pick.

painPoints.pain: The slim center column of a travel tripod slips or shakes with more than an R6 and a standard zoom
painPoints.details: DPReview R6 owners keep a Peak Design-type travel tripod to the body and a standard zoom, little wind, and the column down.

quotes.text: The extending skinny center column can slip a bit under very heavy load.

painPoints.pain: A light travel tripod feels flimsy for long exposures on a windy coast
painPoints.details: An R6 Mark II owner found the Befree Advanced carbon flimsy in coastal wind and moved to a stiffer Gitzo for 30-second exposures.

quotes.text: it just felt kinda flimsy for long exposures when the wind picked up on the coast

painPoints.pain: Leg locks pick up grit on dirt trails
painPoints.details: The same Canon Rumors owner found the Peak Design leg locks get gritty in the dirt on hikes.

quotes.text: I found the leg locks get gritty in the dirt

painPoints.pain: Thin five-section legs flex for night and landscape work
painPoints.details: DPReview R6 astro and landscape replies advise against 5-section legs or thin bottom tubes.

quotes.text: Try to avoid 5 section legs, or 4 section legs where the smallest tube is less than 16mm diameter.

painPoints.pain: Not knowing how much load rating the R6 and its lenses need
painPoints.details: A DPReview reply sets the rule: take your heaviest kit and add 50% to the load rating.

quotes.text: choose the tripod with 50 % bigger max possible load
